title: On‑Prem Terraform Module Release & Breaking‑Change Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft captures a pragmatic playbook for releasing Terraform modules used in Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments. Focus areas: semantic versioning rules, registry publishing steps (internal/private registry), explicit breaking‑change checklist, automation hooks, and an upgrade/rollback plan customers and SREs can follow.

Scope:
- Applies to all terraform modules under github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules that are consumed by Private deployments (vpc packages, network, storage, infra bootstrap).
- Excludes one-off demo modules and prototype scripts in /experimental.
- Intended audience: module owners, platform engineers, release coordinators, and solutions engineers doing customer upgrades.

Assumptions:
- All modules use GitHub flow and are published from the main branch tag points.
- CI produces module bundles and runs unit tests and plan checks before publishing.
- Private registry supports versioned uploads and immutable tags.

High‑level policy / SemVer guidance:
- We follow Semantic Versioning for module releases (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) but with stricter interpretation for modules used in customer on‑prem installs:
  - PATCH: bug fixes, docs, nonfunctional metadata changes. No config changes.
  - MINOR: backward compatible features, new optional variables (with sensible defaults), new outputs. Should include migration examples.
  - MAJOR: any change that removes or renames variables/outputs, changes default values that impact behavior, changes resource addresses or state shape (i.e., requires state migration).
- Every MAJOR must have an explicit migration plan and state change walkthrough in the PR body.

Defining a "breaking change":
- Changing variable name or type (string -> list) is breaking.
- Removing resource or changing resource identifiers that alter state schema is breaking.
- Changing lifecycle or resource creation order that can cause resource replacement without a controlled migration.
- Non‑breaking if compatible with prior defaults and optional flagging is provided.

Pre‑publish checklist (module owner must complete):
- [ ] Create a PR with clear summary and changelog fragment under /changelog/.
- [ ] Add tests: unit, formatter check, 'terraform init & plan' in CI against example/ directory.
- [ ] Update README with upgrade notes if MINOR or MAJOR.
- [ ] If MAJOR: draft migration guide + state-migration terraform snippets and runbook.
- [ ] Add automated linting (tflint/tfsec) fixes or justify exceptions.
- [ ] Add a 'compatibility shim' or opt-out variable for customers where feasible.
- [ ] Link relevant customer issues (Jira keys) and include contact list for customers who may be affected.

CI / Automation steps (recommended):
- Branch -> open PR. GitHub Actions workflow: modules/validate.yaml runs unit tests, fmt, tflint, and runs a 'plan' against example fixtures.
- Label PRs with: module, semver:[patch|minor|major], release-blockers if any.
- For MAJOR: require approval from at least one platform engineer and one SRE.
- Release job modules/release.yaml triggers on merge to main + tag pattern v* and performs: generate changelog, build module bundle, sign artifact, upload to internal registry, and create a release note.

Registry publishing procedure (internal/private registry):
- Only CI release jobs may publish. Manual uploads are discouraged except for emergency hotfixes and must be recorded in the release ticket.
- Steps:
  1) Ensure tag vX.Y.Z exists on main.
  2) CI job builds the module package and runs smoke 'init/plan' against a canonical fixture for the current terraform version used by Private.
  3) Upload package to internal-registry.redwood.ai/modules/<module-name>/vX.Y.Z.tar.gz.
  4) Update internal catalog index and set metadata: published_by, sha256, tf_versions_compatible, breaking_change: true|false.
  5) Post a release message to #private-deployments with changelog and targeted customers impacted.

Breaking‑change release flow (MAJOR):
- Stop the normal automated publish. A MAJOR release must:
  - Have a linked Jira migration ticket with stepwise instructions.
  - Have a scheduled change window agreed with SRE and solutions eng for customer upgrades.
  - Be accompanied by a migration helper script (terraform state mv or scripted steps) and tested on a staging copy of a real customer state if available.
  - Publish a deprecation notice for the previous module at the internal registry and set a sunset date (default 90 days unless customer constraints).
  - Coordinate with customer success to notify customers that need hands‑on assistance.

Canary / rollout strategy for Private deployments:
- Canary group: select 2–3 internal test customers or non-critical environments to apply the MAJOR change first.
- Apply using dedicated upgrade job that captures plan output and stores artifact of the plan for audit.
- Monitor: infra drift, service health, latency, and errors for 48–72 hours post upgrade.
- If canary fails, revert using saved snapshots of state backups and consultation with SRE.

Rollback plan checklist:
- [ ] Pre‑release snapshot of Terraform state (encrypted, off-cluster).
- [ ] Backups of critical runtime artifacts (VM images, DB backups) as defined per module.
- [ ] If rollback needed: run 'terraform apply' against snapshoted state and previous module version; follow module-specific rollback notes in migration guide.
- [ ] Post‑mortem and RCA ticket required within 5 business days if rollback occurred.

Customer communication & support playbook:
- Announce upcoming MAJOR changes on a 3-step cadence: pre‑announcement (30 days), detailed migration docs (14 days), final reminder (3 days).
- Provide channel: customers-announce@redwood.ai and scheduled office hours for hands‑on upgrades.
- Solutions Eng to capture customer-specific constraints in the Jira migration ticket.

Example PR template snippet (include in repo .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md):
"""
Summary: (one line)
Semver impact: patch | minor | major
Modules changed: list
Migration notes: (if MAJOR or MINOR)
Testing performed: (unit tests, example plans)
Linked Jira: JIRA-XXXX
Ops contacts: @ava.chen @diego
"""

Operational verification (post publish):
- Smoke test runbook: example/verify-smoke.sh (runs terraform init/plan/apply against a sandbox, checks resources created, runs basic connectivity probes).
- Post‑release checklist: update module catalog page, increment module mapping in private deployment manifests, tag release in CHANGELOG.md.

State migration common patterns and safe techniques:
- Add compatibility wrappers: keep old variable, add new variable, deprecate old variable for one minor release by emitting a TF warning via docs and validation rules.
- Use 'terraform state mv' in migration scripts with explicit resource address paths; always run in a locked environment (state lock).

Risk matrix (quick view):
- Low: PATCH releases — low risk; automated and can be fast‑tracked.
- Medium: MINOR releases — require regression testing against examples and small customer pilots.
- High: MAJOR releases — require canary schedules, runbooks, SRE signoff, and customer coordination.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Decide canonical state snapshot storage location and retention period (S3 vs internal blob store) — ownership: eng-private-deployments.
- Add automated preflight that detects state‑schema changes in PR (heuristic scanner).
- Define exact SLA for migration assistance offered to customers on paid plans.

References / links (internal):
- Internal Terraform registry: https://internal-registry.redwood.ai/modules
- Module repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules
- RFC for semver policy: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-5678

Notes to self / informal bits (keep here while iterating):
- We may want a "compatibility harness" job that runs all candidate module versions in matrix against the latest Private terraform lockfile matrix.
- Conversation with Security: ensure module signing keys are rotated before GA publishes.
- Add a short 1‑page one‑pager for Sales/CS summarizing migration guarantees we offer for enterprise customers.

Distribution: draft to ENG-PRIVATE-DEPLOYMENTS for review. After two rounds of feedback, convert to "in_review" and file an owner signoff for production playbook publication.

-- End Draft --
